events.title: Nvidia Q2 FY27 earnings
events.why_it_matters: World's largest company reports after market close; consensus ~$93-95B revenue on AI accelerator demand and Blackwell/Vera Rubin ramp.
events.what_to_watch: Guidance for Q3, Blackwell/Vera Rubin supply, China export-control impact, and any AI capex commentary.

events.title: Jackson Hole symposium — Fed Chair Warsh's first speech
events.why_it_matters: New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first major policy speech; markets seek clarity on rate path amid reaccelerating inflation and September hike debate.
events.what_to_watch: Any signal on September 16 FOMC decision, inflation tolerance, and whether Warsh confirms or pushes back on hike expectations.

events.title: US PCE inflation (July) — Fed's preferred gauge
events.why_it_matters: Core PCE expected to edge higher, well above Fed's 2% target, reinforcing the September rate-hike debate.
events.what_to_watch: Core PCE m/m and y/y vs consensus; any sign inflation is reaccelerating beyond energy-driven effects.

events.title: US-Canada trade war escalates — 50% tariffs in effect, Canada retaliation Sept 8
events.why_it_matters: US 50% Section 338 tariffs on ~$20B of Canadian goods took effect Aug 22 after talks collapsed; Canada vows dollar-for-dollar retaliation starting Sept 8.
events.what_to_watch: Whether talks resume before Sept 8 retaliation; impact on autos, steel, aluminum, and cross-border supply chains.

events.title: Iran war / Strait of Hormuz closure — Iran-Oman talks
events.why_it_matters: Six-month US-Iran war with Strait of Hormuz closed (20% of global oil trade); oil fell $2 to two-week low on Iran-Oman talks to reopen the waterway.
events.what_to_watch: Progress of Iran-Oman diplomatic talks; any reopening of Hormuz would sharply lower oil; escalation could spike prices.

events.title: OPEC+ September output hike completes 2023 cuts rollback
events.why_it_matters: OPEC+ approved 188,000 bpd September increase, completing unwinding of voluntary cuts; likely to pause after September.
events.what_to_watch: Whether OPEC+ pauses further hikes given Hormuz disruption; oil price reaction to supply additions.

events.title: Fed holds at 3.5-3.75%, September hike debate intensifies
events.why_it_matters: July FOMC held rates but 3 dissenters wanted a hike; June dot plot shifted to one hike in 2026; markets price ~70% chance of September hike.
events.what_to_watch: September 16 FOMC decision; whether Warsh's Jackson Hole speech signals a hike.

events.title: FOMC July minutes — officials saw need for hike if inflation doesn't cool
events.why_it_matters: Minutes showed most fractured policy vote in years, with broad case for immediate rate increase if inflation persists.
events.what_to_watch: How the hike debate shapes September decision and market pricing.

events.title: US CPI (July) — 3.4% YoY, downward trend continues
events.why_it_matters: CPI rose 0.1% m/m and 3.4% y/y, matching consensus, continuing downward trend from 3.8% peak but still above Fed target.
events.what_to_watch: Whether disinflation continues or energy-driven pressures reaccelerate.

events.title: US retail sales — first decline in 9 months (July)
events.why_it_matters: Retail sales posted first decline in nine months, adding to softening economic data and complicating Fed's hike-vs-hold calculus.
events.what_to_watch: Whether consumer weakness persists into Q3 and pressures growth outlook.

events.title: US jobs report (August) — final reading before Sept FOMC
events.why_it_matters: Final major labor market reading before September 16 FOMC; July payrolls were -23K, a critical input for the hike decision.
events.what_to_watch: Payrolls, unemployment rate, and wage growth vs consensus; weak jobs could deter a hike.

events.title: ECB meeting — September 10, possible hike
events.why_it_matters: ECB held rates in July but signaled September hike firmly in play; Middle East war pushing headline inflation to 3.0% in 2026.
events.what_to_watch: Whether ECB delivers first hike since 2023 and guidance on further tightening.

events.title: Bank of Japan — rate at 1%, next meeting Sept 18
events.why_it_matters: BoJ raised to 1% in June (highest since 1995); next meeting Sept 18 outside window but market watches for further normalization.
events.what_to_watch: Any hints of further hikes and yen impact on Japanese exporters.

events.title: China July data — weak industrial output, retail sales miss
events.why_it_matters: China's economy lost momentum in July with industrial output and retail sales slowing on extreme weather and weak domestic demand; analysts bet on extra stimulus.
events.what_to_watch: Whether PBoC/Beijing delivers fiscal or monetary stimulus; LPR held steady for 15th month on Aug 20.

events.title: China LPR held steady for 15th consecutive month
events.why_it_matters: PBoC kept 1-yr LPR at 3.00% and 5-yr at 3.50%, signaling reliance on fiscal implementation rather than monetary easing.
events.what_to_watch: Any shift to monetary easing given weak data; property sector support measures.

events.title: SEC proposes 'Regulation Crypto Assets' framework
events.why_it_matters: SEC's first formal effort to create a tailored offering regime for crypto investment contracts, following March 2026 interpretation.
events.what_to_watch: Comment period and final rule; impact on crypto issuers and exchanges.

events.title: Boeing engineers/technicians reject contract, authorize strike
events.why_it_matters: Boeing engineers and technical workers rejected 'best and final offer' and authorized a strike; talks to resume.
events.what_to_watch: Whether strike begins; impact on Boeing production and supply chain.

events.title: US government shutdown risk — Sept 30 funding deadline
events.why_it_matters: Federal funding expires Sept 30; Senate passed CR to fund through fiscal 2027 but House must still act after August recess.
events.what_to_watch: Whether House passes CR before Sept 30; shutdown odds and market reaction.

events.title: Tropical Storm Dolly brewing in Atlantic
events.why_it_matters: Next Atlantic storm named Dolly; forecasters watching systems that could turn dangerous as hurricane season picks up.
events.what_to_watch: Storm track and intensity; potential Gulf Coast energy infrastructure impact.

events.title: CrowdStrike Q2 FY27 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Cybersecurity bellwether reports after market close; EPS estimate ~$0.29.
events.what_to_watch: Guidance, AI security product traction, and enterprise demand.

events.title: Salesforce earnings
events.why_it_matters: Software bellwether reports; investors watch AI monetization and enterprise software demand.
events.what_to_watch: Guidance, AI agent adoption, and cloud growth.

events.title: Marvell Technology earnings
events.why_it_matters: Custom AI silicon and networking chip maker; closely tied to AI data center buildout.
events.what_to_watch: AI custom chip revenue, data center demand, and guidance.

events.title: Taiwan AI chip export controls to China — TSMC compliance burden
events.why_it_matters: Taiwan's AI chip export controls likely to take effect within 6-9 months; TSMC faces heaviest compliance burden verifying end-destinations for AI chip shipments.
events.what_to_watch: Final rule details, TSMC compliance costs, and China AI supply chain impact.

events.title: Samsung/SK Hynix test Chinese chip tools as hedge against US risks
events.why_it_matters: Korean chipmakers testing Chinese tools (AMEC) as backup, exposing cracks in US export strategy and potential supply chain diversification.
events.what_to_watch: Whether US export controls tighten or Korean fabs adopt Chinese equipment.

events.title: South Korea overtakes Japan in H1 exports on AI chip boom
events.why_it_matters: Memory exports up 277% on AI demand; Korea and Taiwan top Japan in exports for first time on AI boom.
events.what_to_watch: Sustained AI memory demand and Korea's export momentum.

events.title: G20 finance leaders summit — Asheville (preparations)
events.why_it_matters: Global finance leaders descending on Asheville for G20 summit; Xi's 2026 trip to US in focus amid trade tensions.
events.what_to_watch: Any US-China trade de-escalation signals or tariff announcements.

events.title: China heat wave — crop risks and power demand
events.why_it_matters: Heat wave sweeping agricultural regions threatens corn, rice, cotton crops; energy demand rising; contributed to weak July economic data.
events.what_to_watch: Crop damage extent, food price inflation, and power grid strain.

events.title: US Treasury buyback via General Account — yields decline
events.why_it_matters: CNBC report that Treasury could use General Account to fund buybacks sent yields lower, supporting bond prices.
events.what_to_watch: Treasury confirmation and impact on long-end yields.

events.title: World Cup 2026 concluded — Spain champions (July 19)
events.why_it_matters: World Cup ended July 19 with Spain beating Argentina 1-0; economic impact on US host cities now winding down.
events.what_to_watch: Post-event consumer spending normalization.

events.title: US Q2 GDP and June inflation support September Fed hold
events.why_it_matters: Conference Board analysis suggests Q2 GDP and June inflation data support a September Fed hold, countering hike expectations.
events.what_to_watch: Whether data-dependent Fed holds or hikes on Sept 16.

events.title: US Redbook retail sales accelerate — 9.1% YoY
events.why_it_matters: Weekly retail sales accelerated to 9.1% YoY, suggesting consumer resilience despite July retail sales decline.
events.what_to_watch: Whether this momentum continues into August retail data.

events.title: Trump birthright citizenship EO — Supreme Court struck down broader attempt
events.why_it_matters: Trump signed two EOs restricting birthright citizenship for children of foreign government employees, terrorists, and birth tourists, weeks after SCOTUS struck down broader attempt.
events.what_to_watch: Legal challenges and immigration policy impact.

events.title: Apple v. Epic — SCOTUS grants cert, one-day stay granted Aug 12
events.why_it_matters: Supreme Court granted Apple's appeal over 27% App Store fee; Justice Kagan granted one-day stay Aug 12; ruling expected by June 2027.
events.what_to_watch: Oral arguments and any interim rulings affecting app store economics.

events.title: Canada PM Carney says nation 'at war' with US over tariffs
events.why_it_matters: Carney's 'at war' rhetoric and 50% retaliatory tariffs signal prolonged North American trade conflict with broad market implications.
events.what_to_watch: Escalation trajectory and any diplomatic breakthrough.

events.title: China M2 money supply up 7.7% YoY; cross-border RMB expansion
events.why_it_matters: M2 up 7.7% YoY and M1 up 4%; PBoC expanded cross-border RMB operations for multinationals, supporting yuan internationalization.
events.what_to_watch: Monetary policy direction and yuan stability.

top_risks: Fed rate hike in September (70% priced) — hawkish Warsh at Jackson Hole could trigger broad selloff
US-Canada trade war escalation with 50% tariffs and Sept 8 retaliation hitting autos/steel
Iran war / Strait of Hormuz closure — any escalation spikes oil; Iran-Oman talks could also crash oil on reopening
China slowdown deepening with weak July data and no monetary easing
US government shutdown risk at Sept 30 funding deadline
top_opportunities: Nvidia earnings beat could lift entire AI/semiconductor complex
Iran-Oman talks progress could sharply lower oil prices, benefiting consumers and airlines
SEC Reg Crypto Assets framework could boost crypto issuers and exchanges
AI memory demand (Korea memory exports +277%) supports semiconductor supply chain
Treasury buyback via General Account could support bond prices and ease yields
summary: The market faces a high-uncertainty window dominated by Nvidia earnings today, Fed Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole speech Friday, and PCE inflation data — all feeding into the September 16 FOMC decision where a rate hike is ~70% priced. Simultaneously, the US-Canada trade war escalated with 50% tariffs and Canada retaliation due Sept 8, while the Iran war and Strait of Hormuz closure continue to drive oil volatility with Iran-Oman talks offering a potential de-escalation path. China's slowdown and a looming Sept 30 government shutdown deadline add further macro risk.
